title: Neural Network Engine
description: A feedforward network built from raw NumPy — every gradient computed and checked by hand.
question: Could I build a modular neural network framework using only NumPy — while understanding every line — instead of importing PyTorch?
journey: I wanted to know what backpropagation actually computes, not just what it's called. So the rule was simple: no autograd, no framework — every gradient derived and written by hand.
The engine ended up with dense layers, He initialization, SGD and Adam optimizers, and a softmax cross-entropy loss built from the definition upward.
It reached 97% accuracy on MNIST. The number mattered less than being able to explain, at every layer, exactly why the loss went down.

title: HandMobile
description: A gesture-controlled robotic car — computer vision mapped directly onto motor signals.
question: Could hand gestures, read through a webcam, control a physical car in real time with low enough latency to feel direct?
journey: The interesting part wasn't the car — it was the pipeline from a webcam frame to a motor signal, and how much of that had to happen in milliseconds.
Hand landmarks were tracked with OpenCV, mapped to a small gesture vocabulary, and sent over serial to an Arduino driving the motors.
The hardest bug wasn't code — it was a loose ground wire that made 'stop' occasionally mean 'go'.
